name: vale-vscode
description: The Vale linter extension for Visual Studio Code and editors based on Visual Studio Code.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Linting still works, but settings that control which executable runs or trigger automatic synchronization (the Vale binary path, config, sync-on-startup, and Docker image/args) are locked to your user-level configuration, and commands that explicitly run a process (Sync, Show Configuration, Show Readability Metrics, vocabulary add) are disabled until the workspace is trusted.

vale.maxNumberOfProblems.description: Controls the maximum number of problems produced by the server.

vale.trace.server.description: Traces the communication between VS Code and the language server.

vale.valeCLI.config.description: Absolute or relative path to a Vale config file. If not specified, the default search process is used (relative to the current file).

vale.valeCLI.syncOnStartup.description: Runs `vale sync` upon starting the language server

vale.valeCLI.filter.description: An output filter to apply when calling Vale.

vale.valeCLI.installVale.description: Automatically install and update Vale. If false, the vale executable needs to be available on the user's $PATH. And you need an accessible .vale.ini. file.

vale.valeCLI.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the Vale binary to run, instead of the one the language server manages. Leave empty to use `#vale.valeCLI.installVale#` or the copy on your `$PATH`. Ignored when `#vale.docker.enabled#` is true.

vale.docker.enabled.markdownDescription: Run Vale inside a Docker container instead of a local install. Overrides `#vale.valeCLI.installVale#` and `#vale.valeCLI.path#`. Requires a workspace folder on the local filesystem and Docker (Docker Desktop on Windows) to be available.

vale.docker.image.markdownDescription: Docker image to run Vale from. Only used when `#vale.docker.enabled#` is true.

vale.docker.extraArgs.markdownDescription: Extra arguments spliced into `docker run` before the image name, e.g. an additional `-v` mount for a styles directory that lives outside the workspace. Only used when `#vale.docker.enabled#` is true.

vale.valeCLI.lintOnChange.markdownDescription: Lint as you type, rather than only when a file is saved.

vale.valeCLI.debounceMs.markdownDescription: How long typing has to settle before linting, in milliseconds. Only applies when `#vale.valeCLI.lintOnChange#` is enabled.

vale.valeCLI.showMetrics.description: Show a code lens with the document's metrics (word count, reading time, and so on).

markdownEnumDescriptions: Inherits the `minAlertLevel` from the active configuration file.
Sets `minAlertLevel` to `suggestion`, overriding any configuration files.
Sets `minAlertLevel` to `warning`, overriding any configuration files.
Sets `minAlertLevel` to `error`, overriding any configuration files.
vale.valeCLI.minAlertLevel.markdownDescription: Defines from which level of errors and above to display in the problems output.

vale.doNotShowWarningForFileToBeSavedBef.description: Do not show warning dialog that a file must be saved to be linted.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Displays readability problems in the status bar.
Displays readability problems inline with other problems.
Displays readability problems both in the status bar and inline in the file.
vale.readabilityProblemLocation.markdownDescription: Determines where file-level readability problems are displayed.

vale.vocabPath.description: Path to the Vale vocabulary folder to work with add/remove menus (relative to StylesPath). Example: 'MyVocab' will create vocabularies at <StylesPath>/config/vocabularies/MyVocab/

scripts.validate: npm run compile && npm run lint && npm test && npm run webpack
